items.title: Getting in
items.text: How you reach each workspace. Photo and Design open today's editor; Sprite goes through Sprite setup into the Pixel workspace. Sprites also open straight from the Library.
items.mermaid:
flowchart LR H["Home
recent work, Library"] --> N[New] N --> Q{"What are you making?"} Q -->|Photo| P1[Photo] Q -->|Design| P2["Design presets"] Q -->|Sprite| S1[Sprite] P1 --> PW["Photo workspace
Canvas document"] P2 --> PW S1 --> SS["Sprite setup
size, palette, Project, category"] SS --> XW["Pixel workspace
Sprite document"] H -. open from Library .-> XW class P1,P2,PW photo class S1,SS,XW pixel

items.title: One engine under both workspaces
items.text: A workspace changes tools, panels and shortcuts, never the engine. A Photo document is simply a one-frame document.

Brush, Clone, Heal, Masks, Pen, Text"] --> D["Document
Photo = 1 frame, Sprite = many frames"] XW["Pixel workspace

.cpe / .atelier, PNG, sheets"] D --> LB["Library store
IndexedDB"] class PW photo class XW pixel

items.title: What a Sprite is made of
items.text: Aseprite's model: Layers are rows, Frames are columns, and each square is a Cel. Tags name frame ranges; Slices and Tilesets come later.
items.mermaid:
flowchart LR S["Sprite
size, color mode, grid"] --> PA["Palette"] S --> LA["Layers
Normal, Background, Group, Tilemap, Reference"] S --> FR["Frames
each with a duration"] S --> TG["Tags
idle, walk, attack"] S --> SL["Slices
9-slice, pivot"] S --> TS["Tileset"] LA --> CEL["Cel = one Layer in one Frame
empty, normal or linked"] FR --> CEL TS --> LA class S,CEL pixel

items.title: Making a sprite, start to finish
items.text: Plan the Project first so every Sprite shares a size and Palette. Variants loop back into drawing.
items.mermaid:
flowchart LR A["Plan
Project, base size, Palette"] --> B["New Sprite"] B --> C["Draw
Pencil, Line, Bucket, Pixel-perfect"] C --> D["Animate
Frames, durations, Tags, Onion Skin"] D --> E["Preview at 1x"] E --> F["Save to Library"] F --> G["Export
PNG 1x, Sprite Sheet + JSON, GIF"] G --> H["Into the game"] F -. New Variant .-> C class B,C,D,E pixel

items.title: Library: organize before you draw
items.text: One Sprite per thing, with its animations as Tags. One Palette and base size per Project. Names in lowercase: project/category/name.
items.mermaid:

Bap, CastleD"] P --> C["Category
Character, Tile, Item, UI, Effect"] C --> S["Sprite
knight"] S --> T["Tags inside the file
idle, walk, attack, hurt"] S --> V["Variants
knight_red, knight_ice"] P -. shares .-> PAL["Palette + base size"] S -. sorted by .-> LBL["Labels"] class S,T,V pixel

tabs.label: Tools
tabs.search: Search tools, shortcuts, uses (try: shading, tiles, B)

groups.label: Draw
groups.hint: Freehand tools. In Pixel every stroke lands on whole pixels with no anti-aliasing.

groups.label: Shapes & Fill
groups.hint: Lines, shapes and fills. In Pixel they draw with the current brush and ink, snapped to the grid.

groups.label: Select
groups.hint: Selections limit where you paint and what you copy, move or delete. Pixel selections always have hard edges.

groups.label: Move & View
groups.hint: Moving content, flipping it, and finding your way around the canvas.

groups.label: Brush & Ink
groups.hint: Options in the context bar that change how every drawing tool behaves.

groups.label: Color & Palette
groups.hint: The colors you paint with. In Pixel the Palette is the backbone of a consistent style.

groups.label: Layers
groups.hint: Stacked content. In Pixel each Layer holds one Cel per Frame.

groups.label: Timeline & Animation
groups.hint: Frames, Cels and Tags: how a Sprite moves.

groups.label: Tilemaps & Slices
groups.hint: Reusable tiles for levels, and named regions for UI and hitboxes.

groups.label: Sprite & Canvas
groups.hint: Document-level commands: create, resize and set up the grid.

groups.label: File & Export
groups.hint: Saving your work and getting it into a game.

groups.label: Library
groups.hint: Where every sprite lives, organized by Project and Category.

groups.label: Draft (prompt to sprite)
groups.hint: Optional AI step that writes a rough Sprite you then edit by hand. Billed to your own API key.

groups.label: Photo retouch
groups.hint: Photo-only tools that already ship in Atelier.

items.d: Paints whole pixels in the foreground color. Right-click paints the background color.
items.h: Click for one pixel, drag for a stroke, Shift+click for a straight line from the last point.
items.u: Most of your drawing: outlines, details and single-pixel fixes.
items.x: Photo has a Pencil (P) today, but it draws an anti-aliased stroke.

items.d: Soft painting with size, hardness, flow, spacing and presets.
items.h: Pick a preset or set the sliders in the options bar, then drag.
items.u: Painting, retouching and painting on masks. Not used in Pixel.

items.d: Removes pixels to transparent. In Pixel it always removes whole pixels.
items.h: Drag over what you want gone. In Photo, hardness controls the edge.
items.u: Cleaning stray pixels, cutting shapes out of a silhouette.
items.x: Photo version is in Atelier today.

items.d: Scatters random pixels inside the brush area.
items.h: Hold and drag. Larger brush and longer hold give denser spray.
items.u: Texture: grass, dust, sparkles, noise on rock.

items.d: Picks a color from the canvas into the foreground color. Right-click picks into the background color.
items.h: Hold Alt while using any drawing tool, click, release.
items.u: Reusing an exact color without hunting through the Palette.

items.d: Blur averages neighboring pixels. Jumble shuffles nearby pixels randomly.
items.h: Drag over an area like a brush.
items.u: Rarely in small sprites. Blur for quick soft transitions on big art, Jumble for organic noise.

items.d: Adds text. Photo: editable text layers with font, outline and shadow. Pixel: stamps text with a pixel font.
items.h: Click to place, type, style in the Text options bar.
items.u: Titles, labels, UI mockups, damage numbers.
items.x: Photo text layers are in Atelier today; Pixel text is Later.

items.d: Draws a straight line of pixels with the current brush.
items.h: Drag from start to end. Hold Shift to snap to clean pixel-art angles (flat, 45°, 1:2 steps).
items.u: Edges, UI borders, perspective lines, weapons.

items.d: Draws a line, then lets you bend it with two control points.
items.h: Drag the line, then drag each handle, then click to commit.
items.u: Arcs, ropes, tails, smooth hair strands.

items.d: Draws a rectangle outline. Its second state, Filled Rectangle, fills it.
items.h: Drag corner to corner. Shift makes a square, Alt draws from the center. Click the tool again for Filled.
items.u: UI panels, crates, windows, tile blocks.
items.x: Photo has raster rectangle and ellipse shapes today.

items.d: Draws an ellipse outline, or Filled Ellipse as its second state.
items.h: Drag the bounding box. Shift makes a circle.
items.u: Coins, bubbles, eyes, shadows under characters.

items.d: Freehand shape that fills when you let go.
items.h: Draw around an area and release.
items.u: Fast silhouettes and blobs before detailing.

items.d: Filled shape from points you click.
items.h: Click each corner, close on the first point.
items.u: Crystals, rocks, angular UI shapes.

items.d: Fills a connected area of the same color. With Contiguous off, it fills every matching pixel in the Cel.
items.h: Click inside the area. Tolerance defaults to 0 so it only fills exact matches.
items.u: Blocking in flat colors, recoloring one region.
items.x: Photo has Fill selection today, not a bucket.

items.d: Fills with a gradient between foreground and background, dithered so it stays pixel art.
items.h: Drag the direction of the gradient across the area.
items.u: Skies, glows, light falloff. Use sparingly.

items.d: Box selection. In Pixel it snaps to whole pixels.
items.h: Drag a box. Shift adds, Alt subtracts.
items.u: Copying part of a sprite, moving a region, limiting where you paint.
items.x: Photo version is in Atelier today.

items.d: Round selection, snapped to pixels.
items.h: Drag the bounding box.
items.u: Selecting round parts: heads, shields, orbs.

items.d: Freehand selection.
items.h: Draw around what you want and release. Shift adds, Alt subtracts.
items.u: Odd shapes such as a raised arm you want to move.
items.x: Photo version is in Atelier today.

items.d: Selection from straight segments you click.
items.h: Click each corner, close on the first point.
items.u: Angular regions: roofs, blades.

items.d: Selects by color, either connected or across the whole layer.
items.h: Click a color. Tolerance 0 in Pixel selects one exact color.
items.u: Grabbing every pixel of one color, such as the outline, to recolor it.
items.x: Photo version (with tolerance and feather) is in Atelier today.

items.d: Selects everything, clears the selection, or flips what is selected.
items.h: Use the shortcuts or the selection bar.
items.u: Invert is handy after wand-selecting the background to grab the character.

items.d: Softens a selection's edge.
items.h: Set the feather amount before or after selecting.
items.u: Photo blending only. Pixel never feathers, edges stay hard.

items.d: Fills the selection with the foreground color, or clears it.
items.h: Make a selection, then Fill or press Delete.
items.u: Quick blocking or cutting out parts.

items.a: Move (moves the selection or the whole Cel)
items.d: Photo moves the layer. Pixel moves the selected pixels, or the whole Cel if nothing is selected.
items.h: Drag. Arrow keys nudge 1 pixel, Shift+arrow nudges 10.
items.u: Repositioning parts between frames, centering a sprite.
items.x: Photo version is in Atelier today.

items.d: Scale and rotate with corner, edge and rotation handles.
items.h: Drag handles. Aspect lock in the options bar.
items.u: Photo layouts. In Pixel, free scaling smears pixels, so Pixel uses Flip, Rotate 90° and Sprite Size instead.

items.d: Mirrors the selection or the whole Cel.
items.h: Select (or not), then flip.
items.u: Making a left-facing sprite from a right-facing one.

items.d: Turns the selection or Sprite in quarter turns without losing pixels.
items.h: Choose from the Edit or Sprite menu.
items.u: Tiles and items that need four orientations.

items.d: Pans the view without changing anything.
items.h: Drag, or hold Space with any tool.
items.u: Constantly while zoomed in.

items.d: Zooms the view. Pixel zooms in whole steps (100%, 200%, 300%) so pixels stay square.
items.h: Wheel, Z then click, or + and -. 0 fits to view.
items.u: Draw zoomed in, check at 1× in the Preview Window.
items.x: Photo wheel zoom is in Atelier today.

items.d: Pixel Grid draws a line between every pixel at high zoom. Grid draws larger cells, such as 16×16 tiles.
items.h: Toggle in the View menu. Set the cell size in Grid Settings.
items.u: Pixel Grid when placing exact pixels; Grid when drawing tiles.
items.x: Photo grid guides are in Atelier today.

items.d: A small floating view that shows the sprite at 1× and plays the animation while you draw zoomed in.
items.h: Open from the View menu and park it in a corner.
items.u: Always on while animating. Sprites must read well at real size.

items.d: Sets how big the brush is. Pixel offers square, circle and line shapes, starting at 1 pixel.
items.h: Context bar, or [ and ] to shrink and grow.
items.u: 1 pixel for most sprite work, bigger for blocking.
items.x: Photo brush size, hardness, flow and spacing are in Atelier today.

items.d: Turns a selection into a brush you can stamp.
items.h: Select a pattern, make it a brush, click to stamp.
items.u: Bricks, leaves, rivets, repeated details.

items.d: Removes the extra corner pixels freehand strokes create, so 1-pixel lines stay clean.
items.h: Toggle in the context bar while using Pencil.
items.u: Always on for outlines and line art.

items.d: Paints the color exactly as it is. Painting a transparent color erases.
items.h: Choose Simple in the Ink menu (the default).
items.u: Normal drawing.

items.d: Blends a semi-transparent color over the pixels below.
items.h: Choose it, lower the color's alpha, paint.
items.u: Glass, glows, soft shadows on larger art.

items.d: Paints only on pixels that already have color.
items.h: Choose it, then paint freely over the shape.
items.u: Shading inside a silhouette without spilling outside.

items.d: Each pass moves a pixel one step along a color ramp in the Palette. Right-click steps the other way.
items.h: Select the ramp in the Palette, choose Shading, paint over the area.
items.u: Fast, consistent light and shadow.

items.d: Replaces both color and transparency of each pixel exactly.
items.h: Choose it in the Ink menu.
items.u: Editing partly transparent pixels precisely.

items.d: Mirrors every stroke across a vertical axis, horizontal axis, or both.
items.h: Toggle in the context bar; drag the axis line to move it.
items.u: Front-facing characters, icons, shields, symmetrical props.

items.d: Shows copies of the canvas around itself so strokes wrap across the edges.
items.h: Choose X, Y or both from the View menu, then draw over the seams.
items.u: Seamless floor, wall and background tiles.

items.d: How see-through paint or a layer is.
items.h: Slider in the options bar or Layers panel.
items.u: Photo blending. In Pixel prefer solid colors; use layer opacity only for effects.

items.d: The two active colors. Left click paints foreground, right click paints background.
items.h: Click a swatch to set foreground, right-click to set background.
items.u: Keep your main color and its shadow one click apart.
items.x: Photo has a single paint color today.

items.d: The swatches that make up the Sprite's colors.
items.h: Add, delete, drag to reorder into ramps (dark to light). Turn on Palette only to block colors outside it.
items.u: Set it before you draw. A small palette (8 to 32 colors) gives a consistent look.

items.d: Pulls every color used in the Sprite into the Palette.
items.h: Palette menu, then Add from canvas.
items.u: Cleaning up a sprite drawn freely, or one created by Draft.

items.d: Ready-made palettes such as DB16, DB32 and PICO-8.
items.h: Palette menu, then Load preset.
items.u: Starting a Project fast with a proven palette.

items.d: RGB stores any color. Indexed stores each pixel as a Palette number, so editing a swatch recolors the whole Sprite.
items.h: Sprite menu, then Color Mode.
items.u: Indexed for strict retro work and instant palette swaps. Slice 1 ships RGB with Palette only.

items.d: Swaps one color for another across the Cel, Layer or selection.
items.h: Pick from and to colors, set the scope, apply.
items.u: Making recolor Variants: team colors, enemy tiers.

items.d: Adds a 1-pixel outline around all colored pixels, inside or outside the shape.
items.h: Edit menu, then Outline. Choose color and place.
items.u: Making a sprite pop against busy backgrounds.

items.d: Adds an empty layer above the current one.
items.h: Layers panel button or shortcut. Double-click to rename.
items.u: Separate outline, color and shading so each stays editable.

items.d: An opaque bottom layer. Only one per Sprite, and it cannot move.
items.h: Choose a solid background in New Sprite, or convert a layer.
items.u: Tiles and backdrops that must never be see-through. Game sprites usually skip it.

items.d: Folder of layers that hide, lock and move together.
items.h: Select layers, then Group.
items.u: Body parts, equipment sets, effects.

items.d: An image you trace over. It is never exported.
items.h: Layer menu, then New Reference Layer from file.
items.u: Tracing a sketch, photo, or a Draft result.

items.d: A layer made of grid cells, each pointing at a tile in a Tileset.
items.h: Layer menu, then New Tilemap Layer. Uses the current Grid size.
items.u: Levels and maps built from reusable tiles.

items.d: Hides a layer, or stops you drawing on it.
items.h: Eye and lock icons in the Layers panel. On a Group they apply to every child.
items.u: Lock finished layers so stray strokes never land on them.

items.d: How a layer mixes with the layers below.
items.h: Layers panel, or Layer Properties.
items.u: Photo compositing. In Pixel, keep to Normal unless making effects.

items.d: Merge Down joins a layer into the one below. Flatten joins all layers.
items.h: Layer menu.
items.u: Before exporting a single-layer asset, or to simplify.

items.d: Copies the layer with all its Cels.
items.h: Layers panel button or right-click menu.
items.u: Trying a change without losing the original.

items.d: Name, opacity and blend mode in one dialog.
items.h: Double-click the layer or use the shortcut.
items.u: Renaming and tuning a layer quickly.

items.d: A mask hides parts of a layer without erasing them. Clipping shows a layer only where the layer below has pixels.
items.h: Layers panel MASK section. Paint white to reveal, erase to hide.
items.u: Photo compositing. Pixel uses Lock Alpha instead.

items.d: A grid with Layers as rows and Frames as columns. Each square is a Cel.
items.h: Click a square to edit that Layer at that Frame. Drag to select ranges.
items.u: Any time a Sprite has more than one Frame.

items.d: Adds a Frame after the current one, copying its Cels.
items.h: Shortcut or the + in the Timeline. New Empty Frame adds a blank one.
items.u: Building an animation pose by pose.

items.d: Copies or removes the selected Frames.
items.h: Right-click a Frame number.
items.u: Holding a pose longer, trimming a loop.

items.d: How long each Frame shows, in milliseconds.
items.h: Right-click the Frame number, then Frame Properties.
items.u: Timing: hold the anticipation, speed through the swing.

items.d: Steps through Frames.
items.h: Shortcuts or Timeline arrows.
items.u: Flipping back and forth to check motion.

items.d: Plays the animation on the canvas and in the Preview Window.
items.h: Press Enter, or the play button.
items.u: After every few frames.

items.d: Name a range of Frames and how it loops: Forward, Reverse or Ping-pong.
items.h: Select Frames, then New Tag. Name it (idle, walk) and pick a color and direction.
items.u: One Tag per animation in a Sprite. Game engines read Tags from the sheet JSON.

items.d: Several Frames share the same Cel pixels. Edit one and all update.
items.h: Select Cels, then Link Cels.
items.u: Parts that do not move, such as a body while only the arm animates.

items.d: Opacity for a single Cel.
items.h: Right-click a Cel.
items.u: Fade-ins and flashes without touching the layer.

items.d: Shows the previous and next Frames faintly under the current one.
items.h: Toggle in the Timeline; set how many Frames and their tint.
items.u: Drawing in-betweens and keeping motion smooth.

items.d: Reverses the order of the selected Frames.
items.h: Select Frames, then Reverse.
items.u: Turning an open animation into a close animation.

items.d: A collection of same-sized tiles, like a Palette for tiles. Tile 0 is empty.
items.h: Created with a Tilemap layer; tiles appear in the Tileset panel.
items.u: Any game with grid-based levels.

items.d: Draw Pixels edits what tiles look like. Draw Tiles places tiles on the map.
items.h: Switch modes with the shortcut or the Tilemap bar.
items.u: Draw Pixels to paint tiles, Draw Tiles to build the level.

items.d: How pixel edits affect tiles. Auto (default) creates and reuses tiles as you draw. Manual edits tiles in place. Stack always makes new tiles.
items.h: Choose in the Tilemap bar.
items.u: Auto for most work; Manual when every copy of a tile should change.

items.d: A named rectangle on the Sprite with optional 9-slice center and pivot point.
items.h: Drag a box with the Slice tool, then name it in its properties.
items.u: Stretchable UI buttons, hitboxes, a pivot at a character's feet.

items.d: Creates a Sprite: size (16, 32, 48, 64 or custom), background, Project and Category.
items.h: Home or New, choose Sprite, fill in Sprite setup.
items.u: Start of every asset. Match the Project's base size.

items.d: Creates a Photo canvas from size presets (1:1, 16:9, A4) with a transparent or color background.
items.h: New, choose Photo or Design.
items.u: Photos, graphics and layouts.

items.d: Adds or trims space around the edges without scaling content.
items.h: Sprite menu. Choose the anchor side.
items.u: Room for a sword swing or a taller hat.
items.x: Photo crop and canvas sizing are in Atelier today.

items.d: Scales the whole Sprite with nearest-neighbor, so pixels stay sharp.
items.h: Sprite menu. Use whole-number scales (2×, 3×).
items.u: Upscaling for preview or a higher-resolution game. Downscaling rarely works; redraw instead.

items.d: Grid cell size and offset.
items.h: View menu, then Grid Settings.

items.d: Saves a reopenable project file with layers, frames and settings.
items.h: Shortcut or File menu.
items.u: Always. Exports are one-way.

items.d: Several open documents, each autosaved in the browser and restored on reload.
items.h: Tab bar: new, switch, close.

items.h: File, Export Sprite Sheet. Choose layout, padding and trim.
items.u: Getting animations into a game engine.

items.d: Animated GIF of a Tag or all Frames.
items.h: File, Export, choose GIF and scale.
items.u: Sharing progress, store pages, Discord.

items.d: Thumbnails of every Sprite, filtered by Project, Category and Label.
items.h: Home, then Library. Click to open, right-click for options.
items.u: Finding and reusing assets across a game.

items.d: A game's set of Sprites, with its own shared Palette and base size.
items.h: Create from the Library; pick it in Sprite setup.
items.u: One per game: Bap, CastleD.

items.d: What kind of asset: Character, Tile, Item, UI or Effect.
items.h: Set in Sprite setup; change in Library.

items.d: Free-form sorting words such as boss, forest, v2.

items.u: Cross-cutting groups. Named Labels so they never clash with Tags.

items.d: Duplicates a Sprite with the same size and Palette, linked to the original.

items.u: Recolors, damaged states, seasonal skins.

items.u: A rough start for an idea. Expect to clean it up by hand.

items.d: Sends the current grid back with your note and saves the result as a new Variant.
items.h: Draft panel, Vary, type what should change.
items.u: Quick alternates: angrier face, different weapon.

items.d: Haiku (default, cheapest) or Sonnet (better at following the format).
items.h: Dropdown in the Draft panel.
items.u: Haiku for 16×16 tries, Sonnet for 32×32 and up.

items.d: Shows the estimated cost before anything is spent.
items.h: Read it, then Confirm or cancel.

items.d: Your Anthropic API key, stored only in this browser and sent per request through Atelier's route.

items.d: Copies pixels from one spot to another as you paint.
items.h: Alt+click to set the source, then paint.
items.u: Removing objects by covering them with nearby texture.

items.d: Trims the canvas to a rectangle.
items.h: Drag the area, confirm.

items.h: Adjust & Filters panel, per layer.

decisions.title: Naming decisions
items: **Atelier** is the app. It has two **workspaces**: **Photo** (today's editor) and **Pixel**.
What you make in Pixel is a **Sprite**, as in Aseprite. Product line name: **Atelier Pixel**.
Pixel terms follow Aseprite: Cel, Frame, Tag, Palette, Ink, Tileset, Tilemap, Slice, Onion Skin, Sprite Sheet.
The Library sorts with **Labels**, so they never clash with Aseprite's frame **Tags**.
Open: file extension (.cpe or .atelier) and per-workspace shortcuts. Both are Decision cards on the Board.

terms.name: Atelier
terms.text: One browser studio with two workspaces sharing one engine.

terms.name: Workspace
terms.text: A set of tools, panels and shortcuts for a kind of work: Photo or Pixel. It changes the tools, not the engine.

terms.name: Document
terms.text: Anything open in a tab. In Photo it is a Canvas; in Pixel it is a Sprite.

terms.name: Sprite
terms.text: A Pixel document: size, color mode, Palette, Layers, Frames, Tags, Slices.

terms.name: Layer
terms.text: A stack of content. Kinds: Normal, Background, Group, Tilemap, Reference.

terms.name: Frame
terms.text: One point in time in an animation, with its own duration in milliseconds.

terms.name: Cel
terms.text: One Layer in one Frame: the actual pixels at that spot in the Timeline. Can be empty or linked.

terms.name: Linked Cel
terms.text: A Cel shared by several Frames. Edit one and all change.

terms.name: Tag
terms.text: A named range of Frames with a loop direction. One Tag per animation (idle, walk).

terms.name: Timeline
terms.text: The Layers × Frames grid at the bottom of the Pixel workspace.

terms.name: Onion Skin
terms.text: Faint previous and next Frames shown while drawing.

terms.name: Palette
terms.text: The ordered list of colors a Sprite uses.

terms.name: Color Mode
terms.text: RGB, Indexed (pixels point at Palette slots) or Grayscale.

terms.name: Ink
terms.text: How a drawing tool applies color: Simple, Alpha Compositing, Lock Alpha, Shading, Copy Alpha+Color.

terms.name: Pixel-perfect
terms.text: Stroke cleanup that removes doubled corner pixels.

terms.name: Tileset
terms.text: Reusable same-sized tiles. A Tilemap layer's cells point at them.

terms.name: Tilemap
terms.text: A layer made of tile references on a grid.

terms.name: Slice
terms.text: A named region with optional 9-slice center and pivot.

terms.name: Sprite Sheet
terms.text: All Frames packed in one image, plus JSON with positions, durations and Tags.

terms.name: Library
terms.text: Every Sprite you have, organized by Project, Category and Label.

terms.name: Project
terms.text: One game's Sprites, sharing a Palette and base size.

terms.name: Category
terms.text: Character, Tile, Item, UI or Effect.

terms.name: Label
terms.text: A free-form sorting word in the Library. Not the same as a Tag.

terms.name: Variant
terms.text: A linked copy of a Sprite for recolors or alternate states.

terms.name: Draft
terms.text: The optional prompt step that writes a rough Sprite as a new Layer.

terms.name: Command
terms.text: Every change goes through one, which is why everything is undoable.
